extracted_text: 1. Brixton Prison. Sunday 3. Dec. 44. Dear Comrades, - this is my 3. week of imprisonment. After German & French prisons I now experience a British prison. I wouldn't like to have missed it for worlds! - I have been to Court twice (Police Court, Claphamwell) next court will be on the 9th Dec. At present I am in Brixton Prison Hospital under observation. Magistrate has asked for mental report! Up till now I have not disclosed my identity. I have refused to recognize the authority of the court and to take part in its proceedings. My attitude is a protest action against the state, it's institutions and laws. I will not recognize it's superiority and claims on me. I consider myself an outlaw. The state can imprison me, apply all means of blackmail & legal torture, but it cannot force me to suppress and denounce my own free will. Unfortunately not in the position to destroy the state and it's power! I can, at least, destroy the fiction of it's all-powerfulness, by demonstrating how powerless it is when faced by the determination of a single rebel who refuses to accept it's law. Authority exists only in the imagination. If I do not believe in it, it does not exist! The state can imprison me, but my conception of freedom is different. Restriction of movement does not have to mean restriction of freedom. I am free in spite of prison walls & wardens. My thoughts are free, my spirit is free and no power can break them. The police has so far, with all it's perfect machinery, failed to accomplish the simple task of establishing my identity. Feeling itself ridiculed, I have been warned, in a real Gestapo manner, that I will feel sorry for keeping up my attitude. They expect you to deliver the proof with which they can hang you, and if you don't provide all the data, or as I do, simply ignore them, they are just as ruthless as any Gestapo or G.P.U. agent. The Court told me I will be kept in prison until I disclose my identity. Seeing what little impression that made, they now try to scare me, by putting me under observation. I shall feel complimented if the executors of an insane society declare me mad. There is hardly anything left.
